summary: A fifty-minute mid-week meeting opening with a recording disclosure. Calendar double-bookings are untangled, wins are taken, and pace is checked rep by rep. The setters are released and the closers stay for two call reviews. The first is Michael's John Williamson call from 07/06, where the substantive news is that the deal never landed — the prospect did not answer, then hung up. The second is Andrew's call with a 70-year-old on Social Security, from whom he took a deposit and a 'love it or leave it' trial. The manager teaches the open-wallet-first rule off the back of it, then covers new consumer financing partners. The last fifteen minutes degrade into stories about closing sales while on psychedelics and an extended sexualised exchange about taking clothes off on camera.
notable: THE 07/06 JOHN WILLIAMSON CALL DID NOT CLOSE — this meeting is the only place the outcome is recoverable. Michael before the review: 'I pushed for a deposit, and I think he just freaked out and ran away.' After it: 'Called him, didn't answer, called him today, hung up.' Neither the $100 deposit nor the $6,000 was ever collected. The call record and adherence file for that prospect were corrected on the strength of this transcript.

A DEPOSIT WAS TAKEN FROM A 70-YEAR-OLD ON SOCIAL SECURITY SUPPORTING THREE DAUGHTERS — the prospect on Andrew's reviewed call says 'I would have to be at, oh my gosh, something about half that amount', 'I would have to say I would be more, do something, you know, about the $500 area' and 'I can't, I'm on Social Security and I'm taking care of my family still. I have three daughters.' Chris estimates the income at 'like, $1,300 a month or something like that' and confirms 'It's not much money at all.' Andrew had already taken a deposit and placed him on the love-it-or-leave-it trial, and states plainly 'He said eventually that he won't continue, he won't follow through.' The manager's only correction was process: 'great job getting the deposit, but ultimately open wallet because it would have saved you a lot of time.'

THE LOVE-IT-OR-LEAVE-IT TRIAL AUTO-CONVERTS TO A RECURRING CARD CHARGE BY DEFAULT — Chris coaching Andrew on the mechanics: 'Schedule in a call that they have to attend to again and it's like a decision call... Do that three weeks in, but then still do the follow-ups... and just let them know that if you don't hear from them that it's going to be a recurring payment, it's going to automatically charge their card for the six pay if they want to. If we don't hear from them.' Silence converts a trial into six charges. The same exchange confirms the six-payment plan carries interest: 'if they want to pay in full and do it sooner and avoid any interest, then they can.'

CLOSING SALES WHILE ON PSYCHEDELICS WAS RECOUNTED AS A STORY AND TAKING CALLS ON ACID SUGGESTED AS A JOKE — 'I took what I thought was a microdose, and it wasn't way more than a microdose... And I closed, I closed the guy', 'I mean, it wasn't like a crazy trip, but I was for sure tripping. was like, oh, this is not sober Michael right now', 'I was anxious the whole time because I'm like, bro, I'm definitely high right now.' Chris then says 'We're not doing that anymore.' Earlier in the same meeting, on Andrew taking calls at a music festival: 'Bro, all you got to do is just show up with a hit of acid and you'll be fine, dude.' Andrew: 'Yesterday, we were talking about doing cocaine and beer on the calls.' The recounted incident is placed at a previous company.

EXPLICIT SEXUALISED EXCHANGE IN A RECORDED MEETING, WITH THE MANAGER PARTICIPATING — running from a question about whether a hoodie is professional enough for calls into 'Suck my dick', 'Take off the sweatshirt, and I'll just take off my shirt', 'I can go strip on this couch right now', 'Let's see what we're working with', 'You should start all your calls like that' and 'send in dick pics soon'. Richard then asks 'Hey, Chris, luckily there's no HR department, right?' and Chris answers 'There is, I'm the HR department.' A setter on his first days with the team was present.

NEW CONSUMER CREDIT ROUTES ARE BEING ADDED, ONE CHOSEN FOR ITS APPROVAL RATE — 'We're getting Splitit. So basically, anybody who has a credit card that has $6,000 available limit on it, put them through Splitit because then they'll be able to do it for 0% interest.' Richard adds 'with Klarna, you actually can, to be honest. Klarna does 24 months.' Andrew's sourced lender is recommended on the basis that 'Apparently, they sang in everyone almost' — they approve almost everyone.

SETTERS ARE INSTRUCTED TO DISQUALIFY ON INCOME WITH A SOFT PRICE REVEAL — Derek: 'one of the guys I DQ'd today was a student, and so I just gave him the, hey, it's going to be a four-figure investment, premium coaching, blah, blah, blah, and he was like, oh, that's a little bit out of my price range... Here's the Primal U stuff.' He applies it selectively: 'If it sounds like they're making decent money and, like, they have a decent career already set up, I'm not going to go through with that every single time.' Chris endorses it fully: 'Nailed it... that's like a big part of the job is being the gatekeeper of the calendar.' The unqualified are routed to Primal University.
DEREK HARRIS IS THE SETTER BEHIND THE YOSEF RESNICK CALL — he is on the phones, Adam A. runs DM setting off Instagram and Facebook lists, and Kim Forbes-Sobers is off for the week.

GHOSTING IS RATIONALISED RATHER THAN LOGGED — Chris on prospects who hang up: 'sometimes that's actually a case that you actually had such a great call with them and you did so well that the person didn't want to let you down, but they couldn't move forward. And so they just hung up', and 'everything that happens is essentially a mirror.' Michael: 'people's phones never die before a price drop, ever... if somebody's phone's gonna die, it dies in the five minutes after the price drop.'

COACHING TO REMOVE THE PROSPECT'S EXIT — reviewing the moment Michael asked whether the prospect could transfer funds immediately: 'I wouldn't even ask him that. Um, I would just say, cool. So go ahead and do that. I'll just keep continuing to go forward with getting this all squared away on my end' and 'you kind of just gave them an out. And now you're trying to solve it because you just created the out.'

The assumptive close is held up as the model, quoted approvingly: 'When he's pitching the price, he's like, so here's what you will do. You will pay $6,000. You will give me your Amex credit card. We will get you on the onboarding call, which you will show up to.'

Coaching sourced from an Instagram post: 'Cole had this recent post on Instagram where he talked about closers... They did this weird study and research thing that they found. They move their head the least.' Delivered as a technique for Michael to adopt.

Operational: Michael had a full slate of no-shows the previous day and has started phoning every booked prospect himself to confirm; his sleep is on Colombian time so he is taking calls until midnight. Andrew intends to take calls while travelling to an electronic music festival. Calendar double-bookings put one prospect on two closers' calendars simultaneously, and leads are reassigned manually by the manager because reps cannot do it.
Michael used the word 'retarded' as a pejorative in the meeting, and a joke that 'gingers don't have souls' passed without comment.
